newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt receives 21 bids for seven oil concessions.
newsitem.headline: Egypt receives 21 bids for seven oil concessions.

text.p: Egypt received 21 bids for seven of the 11 oil concession blocks it offered oil exploration companies in its 1996 bidding round, the state's Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) said on Thursday.

"The big achievement is the number of bids from the Egyptian private sector -- at least nine out of the 21 and I'd say that at least two of them are sure winners," said Wafik Meshref, EGPC vice president for exploration.
Egyptian private-sector companies came late to the oil exploration business but now hold four concessions.

Meshref told Reuters he could not reveal all details at this stage but said the companies which have made bids include at least four already operating in Egypt, as well as newcomers from Canada, Argentina and China. The deadline was September 30.
The old companies are Royal Dutch/Shell, Pennzoil, Repsol of Spain, and International Egyptian Oil Company (IEOC), a subsidiary of the Italian company Agip.
He said the Argentine company was Pluspetrol but would not name the Canadian and Chinese ones.
One of the blocks received six bids, one had five and four of them had no bids, he added.
The EGPC bid committee will meet in mid-October to look at the applications for four of the concession blocks.
"First we'll look at the ones where there is little or no competition, the easy things first. Then the ones where the competition is close," Meshref said.

EGPC originally offered nine blocks in the 1996 round, adding up to a total of 154,000 square km (59,000 square miles). They were the offshore blocks of Matruh, North Gharib, North July and the onshore blocks of Siwa, South Dabaa, West Bahariya, West Beni Suef, Assiut and Central Sinai.
Earlier this year it added two more -- Northeastern Desert and North Manzala.
A Russian company had taken the Northeastern Desert block but had to relinquish it because the Russian authorities would not release the money it need to invest in Egypt.
North Manzala, which lies off the northeastern coast, was originally part of the Temsah concession held by IEOC.
